note: Cross-repo contract for the settlement correction (web PARTIAL-REORG). This file is duplicated byte-for-byte in work-address/app (api/src/test/fixture) and work-address/web (api/src/test/fixture); they are separate repositories, so each owns a copy. web asserts it PRODUCES these bytes, this header and this signature; app asserts it ACCEPTS them. A correction names a settlement the marketplace pushed to the settlement route and the app acknowledged, which the chain still holds without a refund recorded beside it: a reorganisation removed a RemainderRefunded mined after the release or dispute refund (MarketplaceEscrow.refundRemainder, its own transaction) and kept the settlement itself. A reversal would unpay a release the chain never stopped holding; the correction takes back the refund alone. The body names the settlement exactly as it was pushed: escrowState is the state it reported (RELEASED or DISPUTED_REFUNDED, the only ones a remainder is refunded beside afterwards), grossBaseUnits, feeBaseUnits, netBaseUnits and refundedBaseUnits its token base units as decimal strings, and txHash its settling transaction, which the chain still holds; correctedRefundedBaseUnits is what the chain has refunded now, less than refundedBaseUnits. The app applies it only while the invoice records that settlement with at least that refund: it keeps its state, payment, hours and binding, and records the corrected refund. issuedAt (unix seconds) and nonce are the replay guard, as for the hire. Every key is always present, in this order. The example corrects the release in marketplace-settlement.contract.json, pushed again with a 10 USDT remainder refunded after it whose block the reorganisation removed. Change both copies in the same pull request or not at all. ROUTE BINDING: every internal route shares one secret, so the signature names the route it was made for. `signature` is the header value, `v2=<hex>`: HMAC-SHA256 with the shared secret over `signedBytes` - the version, `method`, `path`, the header name in lower case and then `serialised`, joined by single newlines - so these bytes signed for this route are refused on every other; neither a settlement push nor a reversal captured on its own route can be replayed here. `legacySignature` is the form used before the binding, the bare hex HMAC of `serialised` alone: app accepts it only while APP_INTERNAL_SIGNATURE_ACCEPT_LEGACY is on, web sends it only as the fallback after a 401 while APP_INTERNAL_SIGNATURE_LEGACY_FALLBACK is on, and both go when that one-release window closes (docs/internal-signature.md in each repository).
